# Appeal of Denial – Bunion Surgery (CPT 28296)

**Governing Policy:** Aetna CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0629.html)

**RE:**
- Member: Quinn Jennings
- Member ID: W670697505
- Denial date: 2026-08-04
- Reference number: POC-6E16FAD700-45453
- Procedure: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
- Payer/Plan: Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Georgia

Dear Aetna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my bunion surgery (CPT 28296), which Aetna denied on 2026-08-04 for "incomplete documentation," reference number POC-6E16FAD700-45453. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already submitted meet Aetna's own published criteria for this surgery. I am asking Aetna to reconsider this denial.

## Why I believe my records meet the plan's criteria

Aetna's policy states that it "considers the following interventions medically necessary" for "Members with clinical symptoms and a history of conservative management who meet the following criteria," including:

> "Bony Correction Bunionectomy Bony correction bunionectomy (e.g., Akin, Chevron, Keller, Lapidus, Mitchell, proximal metatarsal osteotomy procedures, etc.) to treat symptomatic hallux valgus (bunion) in a skeletally mature individual (i.e., after epiphyseal closure) or an individual who is 18 years of age or older when the following criteria is met:"

> "The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following:"

> "Documentation of persistent pain and difficulty walking despite at least six months of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional which includes, but may not be limited to:"

My records show the following, which I believe satisfy these criteria:

- **Persistent pain and difficulty walking:** I have had 24 months of progressive pain in my foot that is not relieved by rest. I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and there is documented ulceration risk over the bony prominence. On exam, I had positive provocative testing on the affected foot and pain-limited range of motion.
- **Conservative treatment under a healthcare professional's direction:** I completed activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic over 10 weeks (2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21, 18 visits), as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-25, which the policy lists as an accepted conservative measure ("Corticosteroid injections;"). Taken together, this treatment spans well beyond the six months the policy requires, and it was directed by healthcare professionals throughout.
- **Skeletal maturity/age:** I am an adult, so this element of the criteria is met.
- **Imaging findings:** Weight-bearing radiographs from 2026-06-29 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees, consistent with the symptomatic hallux valgus the policy describes.

The policy also references arthrodesis and fusion as the preferred treatment in specific circumstances — for example, where there has been "a failed Keller bunionectomy," "advanced degenerative joint disease," "advanced hallux valgus (IMA greater than 20 degrees, HVA greater than 40 degrees)," or "failed cheilectomy." My records do not show any of those circumstances: I have not had a prior Keller bunionectomy, cheilectomy, or fusion, and my intermetatarsal angle (17 degrees) does not meet the "IMA greater than 20 degrees" threshold the policy describes for that alternative pathway. Because CPT 28296 is a bunionectomy rather than a fusion, I do not believe these arthrodesis-specific criteria apply to my case, and I don't understand them to be the basis for a documentation gap.

I did not find, in the policy language available to me, a specific list defining what "minimum follow-up was at least 12 months" refers to in the context of a first-time authorization request, so I am not able to address that phrase further here. If Aetna is applying it as a requirement for my case, I would ask for clarification of how it applies before or during this appeal so that I can respond directly.

## What I am asking

I am asking Aetna to reconsider the denial of CPT 28296 in light of the conservative-treatment history, imaging findings, and exam findings summarized above, which I believe are consistent with Aetna's own medical necessity criteria for bony correction bunionectomy. If any specific document is still considered missing, please let me know exactly what is needed so my surgeon's office can provide it promptly.

I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-01-31, though I recognize the date on my denial letter governs the deadline, and I am submitting this well in advance. I will submit this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form through my account at aetna.com, and/or by fax to 859-425-3379, and I will confirm the correct appeal address printed on my denial letter before mailing anything.

Please contact me if you need any additional information.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Quinn Jennings
Member ID: W670697505
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
